findings.kind: product defect (fixed in the commit that adds this record)
findings.summary: graph deliver-result reused the implementation's deliveryContent for the repaired redelivery, so repair commit 975a0a29 was titled 'feat: add RFC396 finite clamp implementation and tests' instead of the repair tool's 'fix: add ci/verified-release.json with exact src/clamp.cjs SHA-256'.
findings.fix: graph deliver-result: a redelivery of an already delivered implementation round with a different candidate takes the validated development.issue-handling deliveryContent (latest repair); first deliveries and new implementation rounds keep the implementation content; replays keep the saved content (platformWorkItems.ts, graphDeliveryBridge.ts; regression tests in tests/rfc396-mr-bridge.test.ts).

findings.summary: Designer round 3 referenced three element ids it did not define; validation blocked the import and the Case until the operator resumed.
Implementer ran git fsck --lost-found, writing into the protected git metadata root; the guard blocked the round.

The real designer attached post-delivery checks (first CI failure, care repair, evidence, merge decision) to the implementation basis as manual obligations, which can never pass before delivery; the operator must freeze a basis of pre-delivery obligations. Post-delivery steps are owned by MR care, not by graph obligations.
The harness's 8-minute node timeout was too short for real designer rounds with clarification; the product default is 30 minutes.
